perspectives.label: Theoretical Computer Scientist
perspectives.comment: The inherent complexity of SAT/CSP is a fundamental limit on computation.

perspectives.label: Algorithm Designer
perspectives.comment: Algorithm designers are bound by the limits of computational complexity.

commentary.narrative_context: Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) and Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP) represent the fundamental challenge of finding a set of values that satisfy a collection of constraints. Their inherent computational complexity, specifically NP-completeness, is a fundamental limitation in computer science. This constraint limits the efficiency of algorithms and the scalability of solutions for a wide range of problems.
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness is low as the complexity is a fundamental limit, not an exploitable resource. Suppression is negligible as alternative approaches exist, though they don't overcome the complexity class. Theater ratio is near zero as there is little performative activity related to the constraint.
commentary.perspectival_gap: Both perspectives view SAT/CSP complexity as a fundamental limit. The theoretical computer scientist studies the limit, and the algorithm designer must work within it.
commentary.directionality_logic: No beneficiaries or victims as the constraint is a fundamental limit.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: This constraint is not a case of mislabeling coordination as extraction. It is a fundamental limit on computation.
